title: AES cipher path: XMALLOC per setkey then XMALLOC context copy into init_op — redundant copy chain
description: The AES path allocates Crypto2DevAesCtx (32+4 bytes) on wc_AesSetKey via XMALLOC. On each encrypt/decrypt in crypto2dev_cipher(), it then copies those 32 bytes into init_op.key via XMEMCPY, then calls ioctl which copies init_op (240 bytes) to the kernel. So per-AES-GCM-encrypt the hot path does: one XMALLOC (at setkey, amortized), one 32-byte memcpy (key into init_op), one ioctl copying 240 bytes. The XMALLOC is fine (amortized). However: the Crypto2DevAesCtx struct could be eliminated entirely if the key bytes were stored directly in aes->devCtx as an opaque handle (e.g., the key fd if using KEY fd path, or just re-reading from aes->key directly). The current design adds an unnecessary indirection and heap allocation for every AES object. For TLS record processing with short-lived Aes structs, this is a malloc/free per connection for the key context.
